summary.text: Gus Bilirakis is the Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 12th Congressional District and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.
A lawyer who owned an estate-planning practice, he served in the Florida House of Representatives from 1999 to 2007 before his election to Congress in 2006.
He chairs the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade.

paragraphs.text: Bilirakis was born in Gainesville, Florida, and graduated from Tarpon Springs High School, then attended St. Petersburg Junior College, according to Ballotpedia.
He earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida in 1986 and a law degree from Stetson Law School in 1989.

Before entering Congress he owned a law practice focused on estate planning, and he served on the board of Lighthouse for the Blind, as a member of the Rotary Club, and in his local chamber of commerce.
Bilirakis served in the Florida House of Representatives, representing District 48, from 1999 to 2007.

He was first elected to the U.S. House on November 7, 2006, and represented Florida's 9th District from 2007 to 2013 before moving to the 12th District, which includes all of Citrus and Hernando counties and most of Pasco County. In his Ballotpedia survey he names his father, former Rep. Mike Bilirakis, as his hero.
He is a senior member of the Energy and Commerce Committee and chairs its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade Subcommittee; he also sits on the Health and Communications and Technology subcommittees.

His congressional website says 78 provisions he authored have been signed into law and that the Center for Effective Lawmaking at Vanderbilt University ranked him the 31st most effective lawmaker in Congress.
According to his campaign website, he ran on his record of delivering federal funding and on lowering costs.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 52.7% of the vote to Kimberly Overman's 45.9%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
